1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/brainstore"
7		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/factstore"
8		bmanifest "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/manifest"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	)
14	
15	// retrieve.go is the unified retrieval layer behind the qmd-inspired verbs
16	// (search/vsearch/query). It ranks across the brain's text layers — facts,
17	// history, docs — and merges the per-source ranked lists with RRF. Each layer
18	// keeps its own best ranker; RRF fuses them by rank so their incomparable raw
19	// scores don't fight.
20	
21	type unifiedResult struct {
22		Source               string            `json:"source"` // fact | fact-review | history | conversation | doc | consolidation | theme | workspace_pattern | workspace_graph
23		ID                   string            `json:"id"`     // prefixed, addressable by get/multi-get
24		Path                 string            `json:"path,omitempty"`
25		Heading              string            `json:"heading,omitempty"`
26		Line                 int               `json:"line,omitempty"`
27		Text                 string            `json:"text"`
28		Score                float64           `json:"score,omitempty"` // omitted for unranked results (get/multi-get); RRF scores are always > 0
29		VerificationRequired bool              `json:"verification_required,omitempty"`
30		Caveats              []retrievalCaveat `json:"caveats,omitempty"`
31		RelatedIDs           []string          `json:"related_ids,omitempty"`
32	
33		// Source provenance; available fields vary by source. Fact timestamps
34		// retain their distinct creation and revision meanings.
35		EndLine   int    `json:"end_line,omitempty"` // inclusive 1-based source range end
36		Branch    string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
37		SessionID string `json:"session_id,omitempty"`
38		Agent     string `json:"agent,omitempty"`
39		CreatedAt string `json:"created_at,omitempty"`
40		UpdatedAt string `json:"updated_at,omitempty"`
41		Truncated bool   `json:"truncated,omitempty"` // expanded/projected text is bounded, not complete
42		// MatchedTerms lists the query tokens that actually hit this record, so a
43		// weak match is diagnosable instead of opaque (conversation search only).
44		MatchedTerms []string `json:"matched_terms,omitempty"`
45	
46		// Session navigation (additive; conversation source only).
47		SessionRef      string             `json:"session_ref,omitempty"`
48		TargetID        string             `json:"target_id,omitempty"`
49		ContextBefore   int                `json:"context_before,omitempty"`
50		ContextAfter    int                `json:"context_after,omitempty"`
51		OmittedBefore   int                `json:"omitted_before,omitempty"`
52		OmittedAfter    int                `json:"omitted_after,omitempty"`
53		Turns           []conversationTurn `json:"turns,omitempty"`
54		NextTurn        int                `json:"next_turn,omitempty"`
55		PacketTruncated bool               `json:"packet_truncated,omitempty"`
56	
57		// Abstract status on session outlines (additive; never a generation
58		// call).
59		AbstractStatus string           `json:"abstract_status,omitempty"`
60		AbstractIssue  string           `json:"abstract_issue,omitempty"`
61		Abstract       *sessionAbstract `json:"abstract,omitempty"`
62	
63		// Multi-concept session coverage (additive; heading session_coverage).
64		Concepts          []string       `json:"concepts,omitempty"`
65		ConceptMatches    []conceptMatch `json:"concept_matches,omitempty"`
66		EvidenceIDs       []string       `json:"evidence_ids,omitempty"`
67		WorstRank         int            `json:"worst_rank,omitempty"`
68		RankSum           int            `json:"rank_sum,omitempty"`
69		Approximate       bool           `json:"approximate,omitempty"`
70		ResponseTruncated bool           `json:"response_truncated,omitempty"`
71	}
72	
73	type retrievalMode int
74	
75	const (
76		modeLexical retrievalMode = iota // search
77		modeVector                       // vsearch
78		modeHybrid                       // query
79	)
80	
81	// retrievalOptions is the shared retrieval-options contract; extend it
82	// rather than widening positional signatures (cross-cutting rule of the
83	// conversational-memory plan).
84	type retrievalOptions struct {
85		// Source selects the layer(s) to rank: "" or "all" is the default set.
86		Source string
87		// Recency turns on time-weighted ranking: a soft multiplier on the fused
88		// score, never a filter. Off by default because switching it on silently
89		// would reorder every existing caller's results for a reason they never
90		// asked about. RecencyHalfLife overrides the default; zero uses it.
91		// See recency.go.
92		Recency         bool
93		RecencyHalfLife time.Duration
94		// Now is the clock recency measures age against. Zero means time.Now;
95		// tests set it so a ranking assertion is not a race with the wall clock.
96		Now time.Time
97		// Structured conversation-source filters (Phase 2). Zero values mean no
98		// filter. After/Before bound the session time (After inclusive, Before
99		// exclusive); records without a session time are excluded whenever a time
100		// filter is set, so a filter can never leak an unprovable record into
101		// scope. SessionID and Agent are exact (Agent case-insensitive) matches.
102		// Branch filters on the captured branch. All five apply only when
103		// Source == "conversation"; supplying After/Before/SessionID/Agent with
104		// another source is a structured error, never silently ignored.
105		After     time.Time
106		Before    time.Time
107		SessionID string
108		Agent     string
109		Branch    string
110		// Concepts are the additional multi-concept queries (one to four,
111		// joined with the primary query for session-scoped AND coverage). Valid
112		// only with Source == "conversation".
113		Concepts []string
114		// IncludeAbstract adds a bounded top-level preview envelope after ranking.
115		// It never changes rank and never invokes a provider.
116		IncludeAbstract bool
117		// GlobalFacts are facts recorded outside any repository. They are merged
118		// into the fact layer before ranking and go through every filter and the
119		// same scoring as repository facts, so a preference recorded once applies
120		// everywhere rather than only on the CLI surface that loaded it. Callers
121		// that should not see them (--no-global, ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_GLOBAL_FACTS)
122		// simply leave this nil.
123		GlobalFacts []factRecord
124		// NoGlobalFacts is the per-request off switch, matching recall's
125		// --no-global. The environment switch is checked alongside it.
126		NoGlobalFacts bool
127	}
128	
129	// hasConversationOnlyFilters reports filters that have no meaning outside the
130	// conversation source. Branch is excluded: it is a long-standing facts-branch
131	// selector on every retrieval surface and doubles as the conversation branch
132	// filter when that source is selected.
133	func (o retrievalOptions) hasConversationOnlyFilters() bool {
134		return !o.After.IsZero() || !o.Before.IsZero() ||
135			strings.TrimSpace(o.SessionID) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(o.Agent) != "" ||
136			len(o.Concepts) > 0
137	}
138	
139	// parseRetrievalTimeFilter parses a time filter: RFC3339 or a plain
140	// YYYY-MM-DD day (interpreted as UTC midnight). Empty means unset.
141	func parseRetrievalTimeFilter(value string) (time.Time, error) {
142		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
143		if value == "" {
144			return time.Time{}, nil
145		}
146		if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value); err == nil {
147			return t, nil
148		}
149		if t, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", value); err == nil {
150			return t, nil
151		}
152		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("time filter must be RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD (got %q)", value)
153	}
154	
155	// parseRetrievalSource validates a user/client-supplied source selector,
156	// normalizing "" to "all".
157	func parseRetrievalSource(value string) (string, error) {
158		source := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
159		switch source {
160		case "":
161			return brainstore.RetrievalSourceAll, nil
162		case brainstore.RetrievalSourceAll, brainstore.RetrievalSourceFact, brainstore.RetrievalSourceHistory, brainstore.RetrievalSourceConversation, brainstore.RetrievalSourceDoc:
163			return source, nil
164		default:
165			return "", fmt.Errorf("source must be one of all, fact, history, conversation, doc (got %q)", value)
166		}
167	}
168	
169	// retrieveUnified ranks across facts + history + docs, lexically: BM25 for
170	// facts (facts_bm25.go), BM25/FTS with an in-memory fallback for history and
171	// docs. Semantic retrieval was removed (trail #278), so every mode ranks the
172	// same way; vsearch and --semantic survive only as compatibility aliases.
173	// Missing layers are skipped, not errors.
174	func retrieveUnified(repoDir, brainDir, branch, query string, limit int, mode retrievalMode) ([]unifiedResult, error) {
175		return retrieveUnifiedWithOptions(repoDir, brainDir, branch, query, limit, mode, retrievalOptions{})
176	}
177	
178	// errConversationVectorUnsupported answers a direct modeVector call on the
179	// conversation source. No surface produces modeVector anymore (the
180	// verbs alias to the lexical ranking); this guards internal callers.
181	var errConversationVectorUnsupported = errors.New(`vector search was removed with semantic retrieval (trail #278); use query --source conversation for lexical recall`)
182	
183	func retrieveUnifiedWithOptions(repoDir, brainDir, branch, query string, limit int, mode retrievalMode, opts retrievalOptions) ([]unifiedResult, error) {
184		if limit <= 0 {
185			limit = 10
186		}
187		source := opts.Source
188		if source == "" {
189			source = brainstore.RetrievalSourceAll
190		}
191		if opts.IncludeAbstract && source != brainstore.RetrievalSourceConversation {
192			return nil, fmt.Errorf(`include_abstract requires source "conversation" (got %q)`, source)
193		}
194		if source == brainstore.RetrievalSourceConversation {
195			if opts.Recency {
196				return nil, fmt.Errorf("recency is not supported for source conversation")
197			}
198			if len(opts.Concepts) > 0 {
199				return retrieveConversationMultiConcept(brainDir, query, limit, mode, opts)
200			}
201			return retrieveConversation(brainDir, query, limit, mode, opts)
202		}
203		if opts.hasConversationOnlyFilters() {
204			return nil, fmt.Errorf(`after/before/session/agent filters require source "conversation" (got %q)`, source)
205		}
206		includeFacts := source == brainstore.RetrievalSourceAll || source == brainstore.RetrievalSourceFact
207		includeHistory := source == brainstore.RetrievalSourceAll || source == brainstore.RetrievalSourceHistory
208		includeDocs := source == brainstore.RetrievalSourceAll || source == brainstore.RetrievalSourceDoc
209		// Preserve the existing 2x per-layer candidate budget. The facts arm adds a
210		// bounded collapse reserve before applying trust state, so unrelated
211		// history/doc RRF candidates never change merely because a proposal entered
212		// the review queue without converting the entire fact corpus on every query.
213		candidateLimit := limit * 2
214		if candidateLimit < limit { // integer overflow guard for unreasonable inputs
215			candidateLimit = limit
216		}
217		// Exclusion guard: consulted at this retrieval boundary so a
218		// tombstoned session's derived records are unreadable immediately, even
219		// mid-cleanup. Empty guard (the normal case) changes nothing.
220		guard, err := loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, nil)
221		if err != nil {
222			return nil, err
223		}
224		var guardPred func(historyRecord) bool
225		if !guard.Empty() {
226			// Path-based exclusion needs the manifest: blocksFactAnchor falls back
227			// to the transcript path when a record lost its session id, and that
228			// map is populated only from the manifest. Resolve it HERE, before the
229			// facts arm filters below. This used to happen inside the history arm,
230			// after guardFactRecords had already run, so an excluded session's fact
231			// whose only anchor had no session id survived on query/search/vsearch
232			// while brief, dash, handoff, viz, and the pattern corpus all hid it.
233			// Only tombstoned brains pay the manifest read.
234			manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
235			if err != nil {
236				return nil, err
237			}
238			guard, err = loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, manifest)
239			if err != nil {
240				return nil, err
241			}
242			guardPred = func(r historyRecord) bool { return !guardBlocksRecord(guard, r) }
243		}
244		// factstore.Load surfaces corrupt NDJSON as a hard error; propagate it rather than
245		// presenting a broken store as "no results".
246		var all []factRecord
247		var globalFactIDs map[string]bool
248		var active []factRecord
249		var proposals []factProposal
250		var proposalsErr error
251		if includeFacts {
252			var err error
253			all, err = factstore.Load(brainDir, branch)
254			if err != nil {
255				return nil, err
256			}
257			if len(opts.GlobalFacts) > 0 {
258				all, globalFactIDs = mergeGlobalFacts(all, opts.GlobalFacts)
259			}
260			all = guardFactRecords(guard, all)
261			active = make([]factRecord, 0, len(all))
262			for _, f := range all {
263				if f.Status == factStatusActive {
264					active = append(active, f)
265				}
266			}
267			proposals, proposalsErr = loadFactProposals(brainDir, branch)
268		}
269	
270		var lists [][]unifiedResult
271	
272		// Facts.
273		if includeFacts && len(active) > 0 {
274			factLimit := min(len(active), candidateLimit)
275			var reviewGroups []factReviewGroup
276			if proposalsErr == nil {
277				reviewGroups = buildFactReviewGroups(factsEligibleForLocusDrift(active, globalFactIDs), proposals)
278				factLimit = guardedFactCandidateLimitForGroups(len(active), reviewGroups, candidateLimit)
279			}
280			factResults := factsToUnified(rankFacts(active, query, factLimit, false))
281			// Repository proposals and locus checks apply only to repository facts.
282			localFacts := factsEligibleForLocusDrift(all, globalFactIDs)
283			for i := range factResults {
284				if globalFactIDs[factResults[i].ID] {
285					factResults[i].Heading += " (global)"
286				}
287			}
288			if proposalsErr == nil {
289				factResults = guardUnifiedFactResultsWithGroups(repoDir, localFacts, reviewGroups, factResults, candidateLimit)
290			} else {
291				factResults = guardUnifiedFactResultsWithGroups(repoDir, localFacts, nil, factResults, candidateLimit)
292				factResults = annotateProposalStateUnavailable(factResults)
293			}
294			if len(factResults) > 0 {
295				lists = append(lists, factResults)
296			}
297		}
298	
299		// History — BM25 (lexical / hybrid), plus the gated semantic arm (hybrid /
300		// vector; see history_vec.go). The FTS index is an optimization, never
301		// load-bearing (see history_fts.go): on a build/open/query failure fall
302		// back to the in-memory substring scorer. But a corrupt manifest, or a history
303		// index the manifest declares yet is missing/unreadable, is a real storage
304		// problem — surface it rather than returning silently-incomplete results. A
305		// brain with no history source (nil) is legitimately skipped.
306		if includeHistory {
307			// Self-echo filtering happens after lexical ranking. Over-fetch a bounded
308			// reserve so discarded `entire brain ...` tool-call echoes do not leave
309			// the history arm artificially short.
310			historyCandidateLimit := candidateLimit
311			if candidateLimit <= int(^uint(0)>>1)/3 {
312				historyCandidateLimit = candidateLimit * 3
313			}
314			manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
315			if err != nil {
316				return nil, err
317			}
318			if manifest.Sources != nil && manifest.Sources.History != nil {
319				source := manifest.Sources.History
320				// The FTS-payload fast path hydrates its result window without
321				// loading index.json, but it cannot apply an exclusion predicate
322				// during candidate generation and does not resolve the two-tier
323				// duplicate winner. A brain with live tombstones therefore takes
324				// the full path below; an unguarded brain, the common
325				// case, keeps the fast path.
326				if guardPred == nil {
327					// The common BM25-only path hydrates its small result window from
328					// the fresh FTS payload table, then merges the short-term tier.
329					// Legacy/stale/corrupt caches fall back through the verified full
330					// JSON index and substring scorer.
331					scored, _, _, rankErr := rankFreshHistoryLexicalFromSource(brainDir, source, "history", query, historyCandidateLimit)
332					if rankErr != nil {
333						return nil, fmt.Errorf("load history index: %w", rankErr)
334					}
335					scored = filterHistoryRetrievalSelfEchoes(scored, query)
336					if len(scored) > candidateLimit {
337						scored = scored[:candidateLimit]
338					}
339					if len(scored) > 0 {
340						lists = append(lists, historyToUnified(scored))
341					}
342				} else {
343					fresh, loadErr := loadFreshHistory(brainDir, source)
344					if loadErr != nil {
345						return nil, fmt.Errorf("load history index: %w", loadErr)
346					}
347					// Semantic arms rank the long-term records minus files the
348					// short-term overlay superseded (overlay records have no vectors
349					// until consolidation; the lexical tier carries their freshness)
350					// and minus copies a newer overlay copy supersedes. The
351					// exclusion guard filters both arms; it already carries
352					// the manifest-derived transcript paths, resolved before the
353					// facts arm ran, so records that lost their session id block by
354					// path here too.
355					index := fresh.longTermReconciled()
356					if guardPred != nil {
357						index = historyIndex{GeneratedAt: index.GeneratedAt, Records: filterHistoryRecords(index.Records, guardPred)}
358					}
359					scored := rankFreshHistory(fresh, "history", query, historyCandidateLimit, guardPred, func(longTerm historyIndex, eligible func(historyRecord) bool) ([]scoredHistoryRecord, bool) {
360						lex, complete, ok := rankHistoryViaFTSFiltered(brainDir, longTerm, "history", query, historyCandidateLimit, historyFTSRelevanceCutoff, eligible)
361						return lex, ok && complete
362					})
363					scored = filterHistoryRetrievalSelfEchoes(scored, query)
364					if len(scored) > candidateLimit {
365						scored = scored[:candidateLimit]
366					}
367					if len(scored) > 0 {
368						lists = append(lists, historyToUnified(scored))
369					}
370				}
371			}
372		}
373	
374		// Docs — lexical (search/query) and/or vector (vsearch/query). In hybrid mode
375		// docs join BOTH arms, mirroring facts. A never-built doc index is skipped; a
376		// corrupt/unreadable one is a real storage problem and is surfaced.
377		var docIdx docIndex
378		var derr error
379		if includeDocs {
380			docIdx, derr = loadDocIndex(brainDir)
381		} else {
382			derr = os.ErrNotExist
383		}
384		switch {
385		case derr == nil && len(docIdx.Records) > 0:
386			// FTS is an optimization, never load-bearing: fall back to the in-memory
387			// lexical scorer so docs don't vanish when the doc FTS index can't open.
388			scored, ok := rankDocsViaFTS(brainDir, docIdx, query, candidateLimit)
389			if !ok {
390				scored = rankDocsLexical(docIdx, query, candidateLimit)
391			}
392			if len(scored) > 0 {
393				lists = append(lists, docsToUnified(scored))
394			}
395		case includeDocs && derr != nil && os.IsNotExist(derr):
396			// A doc index the manifest DECLARES and the store no longer holds is
397			// data loss, not an un-built layer, and skipping it silently is how
398			// `vsearch` answered "no results for \"Greet\"" with exit 0 over a brain
399			// that had returned six doc hits for that exact query minutes earlier —
400			// while `search`, which reaches history first, exited 1. Two retrieval
401			// verbs disagreeing about the same broken brain is itself the defect, so
402			// both fail here, and for the reason the comment above already gave: a
403			// real storage problem is surfaced.
404			//
405			// A brain whose manifest declares NO docs source keeps the silent skip.
406			// That is a brain that has not been refreshed, not a broken one.
407			if defect := inspectBrainDeclaredIndex(brainDir, brainstore.DeclaredIndexDocs); !defect.OK() {
408				return nil, defect
409			}
410		case derr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(derr):
411			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load doc index: %w", derr)
412		}
413	
414		fusionLimit := limit
415		if opts.Recency {
416			// Retain every candidate through weighting: a fresh result below the
417			// raw RRF cutoff may belong in the final page. The sum is an upper
418			// bound on the number of distinct results after fusion.
419			fusionLimit = 0
420			for _, list := range lists {
421				fusionLimit += len(list)
422			}
423		}
424		fused := rrfMergeUnified(lists, fusionLimit)
425		if opts.Recency {
426			now := opts.Now
427			if now.IsZero() {
428				now = time.Now()
429			}
430			halfLife := opts.RecencyHalfLife
431			if halfLife <= 0 {
432				halfLife = defaultRecencyHalfLife
433			}
434			// Inspect the full candidate pool: weighting may demote every dated
435			// candidate out of the final page, which is still a successful use.
436			if dated := applyRecency(fused, now, halfLife); dated == 0 {
437				for i := range fused {
438					fused[i].Caveats = append(fused[i].Caveats, retrievalCaveat{
439						Kind:    "recency_unavailable",
440						Message: "Recency weighting was requested, but none of the retrieved candidates has a usable timestamp; scores are unchanged.",
441					})
442				}
443			}
444		}
445		if len(fused) > limit {
446			fused = fused[:limit]
447		}
448		return fused, nil
449	}

451	func filterHistoryRetrievalSelfEchoes(scored []scoredHistoryRecord, query string) []scoredHistoryRecord {
452		needle := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
453		if needle == "" {
454			return scored
455		}
456		out := scored[:0]
457		for _, item := range scored {
458			kind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(item.Record.Kind))
459			summary := strings.ToLower(item.Record.Summary)
460			brainInvocation := strings.Contains(summary, "entire brain search") ||
461				strings.Contains(summary, "entire brain query") ||
462				strings.Contains(summary, "entire brain brief") ||
463				strings.Contains(summary, "brain_search") ||
464				strings.Contains(summary, "brain_query") ||
465				strings.Contains(summary, "brain_brief")
466			if kind == "tool_call" && brainInvocation && strings.Contains(summary, needle) {
467				continue
468			}
469			out = append(out, item)
470		}
471		return out
472	}
473	
474	func factsToUnified(facts []factRecord) []unifiedResult {
475		// fact ids are already prefixed "fact:" (factRecordID); history likewise.
476		out := make([]unifiedResult, len(facts))
477		for i, f := range facts {
478			out[i] = unifiedResult{Source: "fact", ID: f.ID, Path: strings.Join(f.Paths, ","), Heading: factstore.KindOrInferred(f), Text: f.Text}
479			if !f.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
480				out[i].CreatedAt = f.CreatedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
481			}
482			if !f.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
483				out[i].UpdatedAt = f.UpdatedAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
484			}
485		}
486		return out
487	}

489	// conversationSessionTopKDivisor sets the default per-session share of a
490	// conversation result list: one session may hold at most limit/2 (min 1) of
491	// the returned results while other sessions still have candidates. Dogfooding
492	// measured single sessions holding 29–84% of a brain's exchanges; without a
493	// cap one long session crowds out every other trajectory.
494	const conversationSessionTopKDivisor = 2
495	
496	// retrieveConversation is the explicit conversation-source arm over exchange
497	// records only, then structured filters and a per-session diversity cap. It
498	// never consults facts, docs, or classified history, and every result carries
499	// the historical-evidence contract. Ranking by mode: search is BM25 (substring
500	// scorer as fallback); query fuses BM25 with calibrated conversation vectors
501	// when the gated semantic arm is available and degrades to exactly the lexical
502	// ranking otherwise; vsearch is semantic-only and returns a structured
503	// unavailable error when the arm is closed.
504	func retrieveConversation(brainDir, query string, limit int, mode retrievalMode, opts retrievalOptions) ([]unifiedResult, error) {
505		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
506		if err != nil {
507			return nil, err
508		}
509		if manifest.Sources == nil || manifest.Sources.History == nil {
510			if mode == modeVector {
511				return nil, errConversationVectorUnsupported
512			}
513			return nil, nil
514		}
515		fresh, err := loadFreshHistory(brainDir, manifest.Sources.History)
516		if err != nil {
517			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load history index: %w", err)
518		}
519		filtered := opts.hasConversationOnlyFilters() || strings.TrimSpace(opts.Branch) != ""
520		// Structured filters are pushed into candidate generation: every
521		// arm ranks only in-scope records, so a valid session/agent/time/branch
522		// match can never be displaced out of a bounded candidate window by
523		// higher-ranked out-of-scope rows. The over-fetch below is dedup/diversity
524		// headroom only. The exclusion guard joins the same predicate: a
525		// tombstoned session is unreadable here even while its derived cleanup is
526		// still running. Superseded duplicate copies join it too: a stale
527		// copy must not even consume a candidate slot.
528		guard, err := loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, manifest)
529		if err != nil {
530			return nil, err
531		}
532		winners := fresh.duplicateRecordWinners()
533		var pred func(historyRecord) bool
534		if filtered || !guard.Empty() || len(winners) > 0 {
535			pred = func(r historyRecord) bool {
536				if guardBlocksRecord(guard, r) {
537					return false
538				}
539				if w, ok := winners[recordReplacementKey(r)]; ok && !sameRecordCopy(w, r) {
540					return false
541				}
542				return !filtered || conversationRecordMatchesFilters(r, opts)
543			}
544		}
545		candidateLimit := limit * 4
546		if candidateLimit < limit { // overflow guard
547			candidateLimit = limit
548		}
549		scanComplete := true
550		var scored []scoredHistoryRecord
551		switch mode {
552		case modeVector:
553			return nil, errConversationVectorUnsupported
554		case modeHybrid:
555			scored = rankFreshHistory(fresh, conversationKind, query, candidateLimit, pred, func(longTerm historyIndex, eligible func(historyRecord) bool) ([]scoredHistoryRecord, bool) {
556				lex, complete, ok := rankHistoryViaFTSFiltered(brainDir, longTerm, conversationKind, query, candidateLimit, historyFTSRelevanceCutoff, eligible)
557				if ok && !complete {
558					scanComplete = false
559				}
560				return lex, ok
561			})
562		default:
563			scored = rankFreshHistory(fresh, conversationKind, query, candidateLimit, pred, func(longTerm historyIndex, eligible func(historyRecord) bool) ([]scoredHistoryRecord, bool) {
564				lex, complete, ok := rankHistoryViaFTSFiltered(brainDir, longTerm, conversationKind, query, candidateLimit, historyFTSRelevanceCutoff, eligible)
565				if ok && !complete {
566					scanComplete = false
567				}
568				return lex, ok
569			})
570		}
571		// complete is only meaningful when the arm actually ran. On ok == false the
572		// FTS/fused arm was UNAVAILABLE (no match expression, open/query failure),
573		// and rankFreshHistory falls back to the in-memory scorer, which filters
574		// the complete long-term record slice and therefore cannot be partial.
575		// Honoring a stale complete=false there turned every FTS outage into a
576		// bogus "filter scan exceeded" error on the default (unfiltered) path,
577		// contradicting this file's own contract that FTS is an optimization and
578		// never load-bearing.
579		if !scanComplete {
580			return nil, errConversationFilterScanExceeded()
581		}
582		// Defense in depth: every arm already generated in-scope candidates; this
583		// re-check keeps the contract obvious and cheap.
584		kept := make([]scoredHistoryRecord, 0, len(scored))
585		for _, s := range scored {
586			if guardBlocksRecord(guard, s.Record) {
587				continue
588			}
589			if conversationRecordMatchesFilters(s.Record, opts) {
590				kept = append(kept, s)
591			}
592		}
593		kept = capConversationSessionShare(kept, limit, opts)
594		if len(kept) > limit {
595			kept = kept[:limit]
596		}
597		out := make([]unifiedResult, len(kept))
598		for i, s := range kept {
599			out[i] = conversationToUnified(s.Record)
600			// Session navigation identity: every hit names its virtual
601			// session so callers can fetch the outline or adjacent context.
602			out[i].SessionRef, _ = recordSessionRef(s.Record, manifest.RepoKey, manifest)
603			// Explainability: which query tokens actually hit this record, so a
604			// thin result is debuggable ("only 'bug' matched") instead of opaque.
605			out[i].MatchedTerms = historyRecordMatchedTerms(s.Record, query)
606			// Preserve list order for callers that read Score; RRF-scale for
607			// consistency with single-list merges.
608			out[i].Score = 1.0 / (rrfK + float64(i+1))
609		}
610		return out, nil
611	}

613	// maxGetBatchIDs caps one get/multi-get request across CLI and
614	// workspace surfaces (the plan's shared result-limit ceiling).
615	const maxGetBatchIDs = 50
616	
617	// errConversationFilterScanExceeded is the structured degraded state for a
618	// filtered conversation scan that hit its candidate ceiling before filling the
619	// requested limit: completeness cannot be proven, so the caller gets an
620	// explicit error rather than a silently partial (possibly false-empty) result.
621	func errConversationFilterScanExceeded() error {
622		return fmt.Errorf("conversation filter scan exceeded %d candidates before the requested limit was met; results would be incomplete, narrow the query or the filters", historyFTSFilteredScanCeiling)
623	}

625	// conversationRecordMatchesFilters applies the structured conversation filters.
626	// Scope safety over recall: a record that cannot prove it is inside a time
627	// filter (no session time) is excluded when one is set.
628	func conversationRecordMatchesFilters(record historyRecord, opts retrievalOptions) bool {
629		if session := strings.TrimSpace(opts.SessionID); session != "" && record.SessionID != session {
630			return false
631		}
632		if agent := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Agent); agent != "" && !strings.EqualFold(record.Agent, agent) {
633			return false
634		}
635		if branch := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Branch); branch != "" && record.Branch != branch {
636			return false
637		}
638		if !opts.After.IsZero() || !opts.Before.IsZero() {
639			created, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, record.CreatedAt)
640			if err != nil {
641				return false
642			}
643			if !opts.After.IsZero() && created.Before(opts.After) {
644				return false
645			}
646			if !opts.Before.IsZero() && !created.Before(opts.Before) {
647				return false
648			}
649		}
650		return true
651	}
652	
653	// capConversationSessionShare enforces the per-session diversity cap: at most
654	// max(1, limit/conversationSessionTopKDivisor) results per session while other
655	// sessions still have candidates. If the cap leaves the list short and only
656	// capped sessions have candidates left, they backfill in rank order; the cap
657	// prevents crowding out, it does not hide the only matching session. An
658	// explicit session filter disables the cap entirely.
659	func capConversationSessionShare(scored []scoredHistoryRecord, limit int, opts retrievalOptions) []scoredHistoryRecord {
660		if strings.TrimSpace(opts.SessionID) != "" || len(scored) <= 1 {
661			return scored
662		}
663		perSession := limit / conversationSessionTopKDivisor
664		if perSession < 1 {
665			perSession = 1
666		}
667		counts := map[string]int{}
668		kept := make([]scoredHistoryRecord, 0, min(limit, len(scored)))
669		var overflow []scoredHistoryRecord
670		for _, s := range scored {
671			key := s.Record.SessionID
672			if key == "" {
673				key = s.Record.Path
674			}
675			if counts[key] >= perSession {
676				overflow = append(overflow, s)
677				continue
678			}
679			counts[key]++
680			kept = append(kept, s)
681			if len(kept) >= limit {
682				return kept
683			}
684		}
685		for _, s := range overflow {
686			if len(kept) >= limit {
687				break
688			}
689			kept = append(kept, s)
690		}
691		return kept
692	}

694	// conversationToUnified projects an exchange record for search results: the
695	// bounded search projection plus provenance and the historical-evidence
696	// contract. Full bounded content is get's job.
697	func conversationToUnified(record historyRecord) unifiedResult {
698		return unifiedResult{
699			Source:               brainstore.RetrievalSourceConversation,
700			ID:                   record.ID,
701			Path:                 record.Path,
702			Heading:              conversationKind,
703			Line:                 record.Line,
704			EndLine:              record.EndLine,
705			Branch:               record.Branch,
706			SessionID:            record.SessionID,
707			Agent:                record.Agent,
708			CreatedAt:            record.CreatedAt,
709			Text:                 record.Summary,
710			Truncated:            record.ProjectionTruncated,
711			VerificationRequired: true,
712			Caveats:              []retrievalCaveat{conversationHistoricalEvidenceCaveat()},
713		}
714	}
715	
716	// conversationGetResult is the bounded ID-based expansion: re-parse the exact
717	// indexed range from the canonical transcript when its digest still matches;
718	// otherwise degrade to the stored projection with a caveat naming WHICH
719	// contract failed. Too-large, stale, and unreadable sources are distinct
720	// states, never one collapsed "stale" answer.
721	func conversationGetResult(brainDir string, record historyRecord) unifiedResult {
722		result := conversationToUnified(record)
723		expansion, err := expandConversationExchange(brainDir, record)
724		switch {
725		case err == nil:
726			result.Text = conversationExpansionText(expansion)
727			result.Truncated = expansion.Truncated
728		case errors.Is(err, errConversationSourceTooLarge):
729			result.Caveats = append(result.Caveats, conversationSourceTooLargeCaveat(record.Path))
730		case errors.Is(err, errConversationSourceStale):
731			result.Caveats = append(result.Caveats, conversationSourceStaleCaveat(record.Path))
732		default:
733			result.Caveats = append(result.Caveats, conversationSourceUnreadableCaveat(record.Path))
734		}
735		return result
736	}
737	
738	func historyToUnified(scored []scoredHistoryRecord) []unifiedResult {
739		out := make([]unifiedResult, len(scored))
740		for i, s := range scored {
741			out[i] = unifiedResult{Source: "history", ID: s.Record.ID, Path: s.Record.Path, Line: s.Record.Line, Heading: s.Record.Kind, Text: s.Record.Summary}
742			// Classic history records carry no time. Leaving CreatedAt empty is
743			// the honest answer: recency treats undated records as neutral, not old.
744			out[i].CreatedAt = s.Record.CreatedAt
745		}
746		return out
747	}
748	
749	func docToUnified(r docRecord) unifiedResult {
750		result := unifiedResult{Source: "doc", ID: "doc:" + r.ID, Path: r.Path, Line: r.Line, Heading: r.Heading, Text: r.Text}
751		if r.Historical {
752			result.VerificationRequired = true
753			result.Caveats = []retrievalCaveat{{
754				Kind:    retrievalCaveatHistoricalDocument,
755				Message: "This document is explicitly historical or superseded; prefer current operational documentation.",
756				Paths:   []string{r.Path},
757				Action:  "Verify against the current README and active implementation before relying on it.",
758			}}
759		}
760		return result
761	}
762	
763	func docsToUnified(scored []scoredDocRecord) []unifiedResult {
764		out := make([]unifiedResult, len(scored))
765		for i, s := range scored {
766			out[i] = docToUnified(s.Record)
767		}
768		return out
769	}
770	
771	func rrfMergeUnified(lists [][]unifiedResult, limit int) []unifiedResult {
772		fused := map[string]float64{}
773		rec := map[string]unifiedResult{}
774		for _, list := range lists {
775			for rank, r := range list {
776				fused[r.ID] += 1.0 / (rrfK + float64(rank+1))
777				if _, ok := rec[r.ID]; !ok {
778					rec[r.ID] = r
779				}
780			}
781		}
782		out := make([]unifiedResult, 0, len(rec))
783		for id, r := range rec {
784			r.Score = fused[id]
785			out = append(out, r)
786		}
787		sortUnifiedByScore(out)
788		if len(out) > limit {
789			out = out[:limit]
790		}
791		return out
792	}
793	
794	// sortUnifiedByScore orders by score descending, breaking ties on id so the
795	// order is stable across runs. Recency reweighting re-sorts with the same
796	// comparison, so a reweighted list and a fused list are ordered by one rule.
797	func sortUnifiedByScore(out []unifiedResult) {
798		sort.Slice(out, func(a, b int) bool {
799			if out[a].Score != out[b].Score {
800				return out[a].Score > out[b].Score
801			}
802			return out[a].ID < out[b].ID
803		})
804	}
805	
806	// getUnifiedBatch resolves prefixed ids (fact:/review:/history:/doc:/pattern:/theme:) to full records,
807	// loading each corpus at most once and indexing it by id. get/multi-get
808	// route through here so resolving N ids is O(corpus
809	// + N), not O(N × corpus) — the latter rescans the full history per id and is
810	// pathological on large brains. Results preserve input order.
811	func getUnifiedBatch(repoDir, brainDir, branch string, ids []string) (found []unifiedResult, missing []string, err error) {
812		return getUnifiedBatchOptions(repoDir, brainDir, branch, ids, getOptions{})
813	}
814	
815	func getUnifiedBatchOptions(repoDir, brainDir, branch string, ids []string, gopts getOptions) (found []unifiedResult, missing []string, err error) {
816		// One request fans out to at most this many record resolutions; each
817		// conversation id triggers a bounded transcript read, so the batch size
818		// itself must be bounded too.
819		if len(ids) > maxGetBatchIDs {
820			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("at most %d ids per get/multi-get request (got %d)", maxGetBatchIDs, len(ids))
821		}
822		if err := validateGetOptions(gopts); err != nil {
823			return nil, nil, err
824		}
825		var wantFact, wantReview, wantHistory, wantConversation, wantSession, wantDoc, wantPatternDerived bool
826		for _, id := range ids {
827			switch {
828			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "fact:"):
829				wantFact = true
830			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "review:"):
831				wantReview = true
832			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "history:"):
833				wantHistory = true
834			case strings.HasPrefix(id, brainstore.ConversationSessionIDPrefix):
835				wantSession = true
836			case strings.HasPrefix(id, conversationIDPrefix):
837				wantConversation = true
838			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "doc:"):
839				wantDoc = true
840			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "pattern:"), strings.HasPrefix(id, "theme:"):
841				wantPatternDerived = true
842			}
843		}
844		if wantPatternDerived {
845			if err := requirePrivacyDerivedRead(brainDir); err != nil {
846				return nil, nil, err
847			}
848		}
849		// Navigation arguments are type-specific: context counts belong to a
850		// single conversation: target, outline cursor/limit to a single
851		// conversation-session: target. Anything else is a structured
852		// invalid-argument error, never an ignored option.
853		if gopts.navigation() && len(ids) != 1 {
854			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("navigation options require exactly one target id (got %d)", len(ids))
855		}
856		if gopts.ContextSet && !wantConversation {
857			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("context-before/context-after are valid only for a conversation: target")
858		}
859		if gopts.OutlineSet && !wantSession {
860			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("after-turn/limit are valid only for a conversation-session: target")
861		}
862		if wantSession && len(ids) != 1 {
863			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("a conversation-session: outline requires its own single-id request")
864		}
865		// Exclusion guard: a tombstoned session's records resolve as "not
866		// found" on every get surface immediately, even before cleanup finishes.
867		guard, err := loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, nil)
868		if err != nil {
869			return nil, nil, err
870		}
871		if !guard.Empty() {
872			// Resolve the manifest-derived transcript paths BEFORE the facts arm
873			// filters below, so a fact whose only anchor lost its session id blocks
874			// by path here too. The history arm's later re-resolution ran after
875			// guardFactRecords and therefore never protected `get fact:`.
876			manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
877			if err != nil {
878				return nil, nil, err
879			}
880			guard, err = loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, manifest)
881			if err != nil {
882				return nil, nil, err
883			}
884		}
885		factByID := map[string]factRecord{}
886		var globalGetIDs map[string]bool
887		var reviewByID map[string]factReviewGroup
888		var reviewByFactID map[string]factReviewGroup
889		var proposalStateUnavailable bool
890		if wantFact || wantReview {
891			// Surface a corrupt facts store as an error, not a misleading "not found".
892			facts, ferr := factstore.Load(brainDir, branch)
893			if ferr != nil {
894				return nil, nil, ferr
895			}
896			if len(gopts.GlobalFacts) > 0 {
897				// query and search return global facts, so their ids have to
898				// resolve here too. The repository's copy still wins on a collision.
899				facts, globalGetIDs = mergeGlobalFacts(facts, gopts.GlobalFacts)
900			}
901			facts = guardFactRecords(guard, facts)
902			for _, f := range facts {
903				factByID[f.ID] = f
904			}
905			proposals, perr := loadFactProposals(brainDir, branch)
906			if perr != nil && wantReview {
907				return nil, nil, perr
908			}
909			if perr == nil {
910				localFacts := factsEligibleForLocusDrift(facts, globalGetIDs)
911				reviewByID, reviewByFactID = indexFactReviewGroups(buildFactReviewGroups(localFacts, proposals))
912			} else {
913				proposalStateUnavailable = true
914			}
915		}
916		histByID := map[string]historyRecord{}
917		convByID := map[string]historyRecord{}
918		var sessionViews map[string]conversationSessionView
919		var abstractResolver *sessionAbstractResolver
920		// convScopes maps a conversation id to its session scopes (ref -> newest
921		// record in that scope), so a legacy id colliding across scopes is a
922		// structured ambiguity, never a silent last-write-wins pick.
923		convScopes := map[string]map[string]historyRecord{}
924		if wantHistory || wantConversation || wantSession {
925			// A corrupt manifest, or a history index the manifest declares but that is
926			// missing/unreadable, is a real storage problem — surface it rather than
927			// reporting every history:* id as "not found". A brain with no history source
928			// (nil) legitimately has no such records, so leave histByID empty.
929			manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
930			if err != nil {
931				return nil, nil, err
932			}
933			if manifest.Sources != nil && manifest.Sources.History != nil {
934				fresh, err := loadFreshHistory(brainDir, manifest.Sources.History)
935				if err != nil {
936					return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("load history index: %w", err)
937				}
938				// The guard already carries the manifest-derived transcript paths
939				// (resolved above, before the facts arm), so records that lost
940				// their session id block by path on every surface here.
941				if wantConversation || wantSession {
942					sessionViews = buildConversationSessionViews(fresh, manifest.RepoKey, manifest, guard)
943					for ref, view := range sessionViews {
944						for _, r := range view.Records {
945							scopes := convScopes[r.ID]
946							if scopes == nil {
947								scopes = map[string]historyRecord{}
948								convScopes[r.ID] = scopes
949							}
950							if prev, ok := scopes[ref]; ok {
951								scopes[ref] = newestHistoryRecord(prev, r)
952							} else {
953								scopes[ref] = r
954							}
955						}
956					}
957				}
958				// reconciledRecords collapses duplicate stable IDs to the same
959				// newest-copy winner ranking uses, so get expands exactly the
960				// record search returned.
961				for _, r := range fresh.reconciledRecords() {
962					if guardBlocksRecord(guard, r) {
963						continue
964					}
965					if r.Kind == conversationKind {
966						convByID[r.ID] = r
967						continue
968					}
969					histByID[r.ID] = r
970				}
971			}
972		}
973		if wantSession {
974			abstractResolver = newSessionAbstractResolver(brainDir)
975		}
976		docByID := map[string]docRecord{}
977		if wantDoc {
978			// A never-built doc index is not an error (doc:* ids just report "not
979			// found"); a corrupt/unreadable one is — surface it.
980			index, err := loadDocIndex(brainDir)
981			switch {
982			case err == nil:
983				for _, r := range index.Records {
984					docByID[r.ID] = r
985				}
986			case os.IsNotExist(err):
987				if defect := inspectBrainDeclaredIndex(brainDir, brainstore.DeclaredIndexDocs); !defect.OK() {
988					return nil, nil, defect
989				}
990			case !os.IsNotExist(err):
991				return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("load doc index: %w", err)
992			}
993		}
994		for _, id := range ids {
995			switch {
996			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "fact:"):
997				if f, ok := factByID[id]; ok {
998					r := factsToUnified([]factRecord{f})[0]
999					if group, pending := reviewByFactID[id]; pending {
1000						r = annotateExplicitFactReview(r, group)
1001					}
1002					if globalGetIDs[f.ID] {
1003						// Not scoped to this repository, so locus drift cannot
1004						// answer for it; labelled the way the ranked surfaces are.
1005						r.Heading += " (global)"
1006					} else {
1007						r = annotateFactLocusTrust(repoDir, f, r)
1008					}
1009					if proposalStateUnavailable {
1010						r = annotateProposalStateUnavailable([]unifiedResult{r})[0]
1011					}
1012					found = append(found, r)
1013					continue
1014				}
1015			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "review:"):
1016				if group, ok := reviewByID[id]; ok {
1017					r := factReviewToUnified(repoDir, group)
1018					// Preserve an addressable proposal alias if the group grew, including
1019					// the machine-readable caveat that tells clients what to review.
1020					r.ID = id
1021					for i := range r.Caveats {
1022						if r.Caveats[i].Kind == retrievalCaveatUnresolvedReview {
1023							r.Caveats[i].ReviewID = id
1024						}
1025					}
1026					found = append(found, r)
1027					continue
1028				}
1029			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "history:"):
1030				if r, ok := histByID[id]; ok {
1031					found = append(found, historyToUnified([]scoredHistoryRecord{{Record: r}})[0])
1032					continue
1033				}
1034			case strings.HasPrefix(id, brainstore.ConversationSessionIDPrefix):
1035				if view, ok := sessionViews[id]; ok {
1036					outline := conversationSessionOutline(view, gopts.AfterTurn, gopts.OutlineLimit)
1037					outline.AbstractStatus, outline.Abstract = abstractResolver.status(view)
1038					outline = boundSessionAbstractEnvelope(outline)
1039					if outline.AbstractStatus == abstractStatusStale || outline.AbstractStatus == abstractStatusMissing {
1040						if err := enqueueAutomaticAbstractReconciliationHook(brainDir, "session_get", time.Now().UTC()); err != nil {
1041							// Automatic generation is an optional acceleration. Exact
1042							// session recall remains valid even when its durable work
1043							// enqueue is temporarily unavailable; expose the issue instead
1044							// of converting a successful get into a failure.
1045							outline.AbstractIssue = memoryOperationalError(err)
1046						}
1047					}
1048					found = append(found, outline)
1049					continue
1050				}
1051			case strings.HasPrefix(id, conversationIDPrefix):
1052				// The transcript path is resolved from the indexed record only;
1053				// a client-supplied id can never choose a filesystem path.
1054				scopes := convScopes[id]
1055				if len(scopes) > 1 {
1056					// The existing branch selector may disambiguate a legacy id
1057					// that collides across session scopes; a silent winner never
1058					// may.
1059					matching := map[string]historyRecord{}
1060					for ref, record := range scopes {
1061						if record.Branch == branch {
1062							matching[ref] = record
1063						}
1064					}
1065					if len(matching) != 1 {
1066						return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("memory_identity_ambiguous: %s resolves to %d session scopes; pass --branch to select one", id, len(scopes))
1067					}
1068					scopes = matching
1069				}
1070				if len(scopes) == 1 {
1071					for ref, record := range scopes {
1072						if gopts.ContextSet {
1073							found = append(found, conversationContextPacket(brainDir, sessionViews[ref], record, gopts.ContextBefore, gopts.ContextAfter))
1074						} else {
1075							result := conversationGetResult(brainDir, record)
1076							result.SessionRef = ref
1077							found = append(found, result)
1078						}
1079					}
1080					continue
1081				}
1082				if r, ok := convByID[id]; ok {
1083					found = append(found, conversationGetResult(brainDir, r))
1084					continue
1085				}
1086			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "doc:"):
1087				if r, ok := docByID[strings.TrimPrefix(id, "doc:")]; ok {
1088					found = append(found, docToUnified(r))
1089					continue
1090				}
1091			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "pattern:"):
1092				// Consolidation dossier addressed by its pattern id (v2). Corpus is
1093				// rebuildable/optional, so a missing corpus is "not found", not an error.
1094				if r, ok, err := getCorpusConsolidationChecked(brainDir, id); err != nil {
1095					return nil, nil, err
1096				} else if ok {
1097					found = append(found, r)
1098					continue
1099				}
1100			case strings.HasPrefix(id, "theme:"):
1101				if r, ok, err := getCorpusThemeChecked(brainDir, id); err != nil {
1102					return nil, nil, err
1103				} else if ok {
1104					found = append(found, r)
1105					continue
1106				}
1107			}
1108			missing = append(missing, id)
1109		}
1110		return found, missing, nil
1111	}

First I want to set up a compile probe by copying retrieve.go into an isolated package and building it to count undefined references, which will help me figure out which pieces are actually movable.

import sys

MOD = "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/"


def ensure_import(path, pkg, qualifier=None):
    """Add import of MOD+pkg to file if it uses qualifier. (or alias) and lacks the import."""
    with open(path) as f:
        src = f.read()
    q = (qualifier or pkg) + "."

    else:
        m = re.search(r'import \(\n', src)
        if not m:
            return False
        src = src[: m.end()] + line + src[m.end() :]
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(src)
    return True


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pkg = sys.argv[1]
    qualifier = None
    rest = sys.argv[2:]
    if rest and rest[0] == "--as":
        qualifier = rest[1]
        rest = rest[2:]
    for p in rest:
        if ensure_import(p, pkg, qualifier):
            print("added", p)

import re
import subprocess
import sys

root = sys.argv[1]
for _ in range(30):
    p = subprocess.run(["go", "vet", "./..."], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = p.stdout + p.stderr
    m = re.search(r'vet: ([^\s:]+):\d+:\d+: "([^"]+)" imported and not used', out)
    if not m:
        print("done")
        print("\n".join(out.splitlines()[:15]))
        break
    path, imp = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    full = root + "/" + path
    with open(full) as f:
        lines = f.readlines()
    with open(full, "w") as f:
        for ln in lines:
            if re.match(r'^\t(?:\w+ )?"%s"\n$' % re.escape(imp), ln):
                continue
            f.write(ln)
    print("removed", imp, "from", path)

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
